title: Research Projects and Interests
text:
Overview of a rhizotron-scale phenotyping study showing a pinto bean root system submerged in water, its corresponding polarization response, and the retrieved correlation between chargeability and root biomass of the investigated plants.


One part of my research focused on establishing a relationship between the tomographic polarization response of plant roots and their corresponding biomass. In a phenotyping study conducted at the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, we could show that the spatially resolved total polarizability of pinto bean, black bean, soy bean and maize root systems is strongly correlated with their corresponding root biomass. This study was published 2024 in Plant Methods.

title: Valentin Michels
text:
Bio
I am currently working as a Research Scientist within the Excellence Cluster “Phenorob” at the University of Bonn in Germany. My research focuses on the use of geophysical imaging methods for environmental, agricultural, and geological applications. After completing my Bachelor’s degree in Geosciences and Master’s degree in Geophysics, I pursued a PhD in Geophysics at the University of Bonn. My doctoral research focused on developing spectral electrical impedance tomography (sEIT) as a field-scale imaging tool to non-invasively phenotype agricultural crop roots.
On this site, I keep a list of my publications and conference contributions, my CV, and an overview of my research projects and interests.
